page.definition_block: Aircraft Structure, Surfaces, Rigging, And Systems Assemblers work in final aircraft manufacturing. They follow drawings and process specifications to assemble, adjust, and test fuselage structures, wing skins, control surfaces, cable rigging, and flight control and hydraulic systems. They sign assembly records and carry front-line responsibility for aircraft quality.

rows.label: Work Environment
rows.value: Aircraft final assembly shops and hangars with paced, mostly standing work in clean environments

rows.label: Education Requirement
rows.value: Vocational or college education in aviation manufacturing or mechanics, supported by qualifications and structured training

rows.label: Key Skills
rows.value: Drawing interpretation, riveting and assembly, tolerance measurement, system adjustment, and quality records

rows.label: Core Activities
rows.value: Structural assembly, skin riveting, rigging adjustment, system installation, measurement, and records

rows.label: Work Values
rows.value: Rigor, responsibility, quality first, and teamwork

rows.label: Entry Requirement
rows.value: Moderate-high: specialized education + assembly qualifications + multiple rounds of controlled training

responsibilities_block: Assemble structural components such as fuselage sections, wings, and control surfaces from drawings.
Install skins, doors, and fairings and complete riveting and fastening.
Route and adjust control cables, linkages, and flight control transmission systems.
Install hydraulic, electrical, fuel, and other onboard system lines and components.
Use measurement tools to inspect assembly tolerances and record assembly data.
Support testing and verify control-system travel and tension.
page.work_context_block: Final assembly runs on cycle time and signatures. Each station has a fixed production rhythm, and assigned work must finish within the specified time. Every completed item receives a signed assembly record. Drawings, gauges, and torque wrenches are standard. If a gap exceeds tolerance, stop and involve manufacturing engineering rather than passing a defective assembly forward.

In the morning, an arbitrator presides over an employment dispute hearing and lets each side explain its position. In the afternoon, private caucuses test limits and identify common ground. In the evening, the arbitrator decides whether to pursue settlement or move into adjudication and draft the required documents.

responsibilities_block: Prune street and landscape trees according to work plans.
Remove dead, diseased, and hazardous branches.
Shape and thin crowns to control tree form.
Address unsafe clearance between trees, power lines, and buildings.
Operate and maintain chainsaws, pole pruners, and other tools.
Remove cut branches and clean the worksite.
page.work_context_block: The day's rhythm is inspect, cut, and clear. First, follow the work order to the site, assess the tree and surroundings, and check for power lines, buildings, and pedestrians. Then climb the tree or enter the lift bucket, cut dead and diseased branches section by section, and warn people below to stay clear. Sort and load branches after cutting and leave the site clean. Wearing protective clothing in hot weather and becoming soaked in sweat is routine, but seeing a well-shaped tree with its hazards removed brings satisfaction.

responsibilities_block: 按计划对行道树与绿化树木进行修剪。
清理枯枝、病枝与安全隐患枝条。
进行树冠整形与疏枝，控制树形。
处理树木与电线、建筑的间距隐患。
操作电锯、高枝剪等工具并维护。
清运修剪产生的枝条与现场。
page.work_context_block: 一天的主旋律是「查—锯—清」：先按工单到现场，观察树况和周边环境，确认有没有电线、建筑和行人；然后爬树或上车斗，一截截锯掉枯枝病枝，喊话让下面的人避开；锯完把枝条分拣装车，场地收拾干净。大热天穿着防护服，汗流浃背是常态，但看到树形利落、隐患排除，还是有成就感的。
